item.text: The first probe shows the original code is permissive in nonstandard ways: overall URL validity and scheme validity are not equivalent, host validation is loose, and path splitting ignores repeated slashes plus query/fragment tails. I’m narrowing the parsing rules now so the Rust parser extracts the same fields.

item.text: I’ve pinned down a workable parse model: strip query/fragment, detect `scheme://`, split authority from path, drop userinfo at the last `@`, only treat a port as separate when the remaining hostport has exactly one `:`, and treat URL validity as “host or path is non-empty.” I’m writing the Rust modules to follow that behavior exactly and keeping the binary buildable both with `cargo` and direct `rustc`.
I’m at the edit step now. I’m creating a small `url_parser` module tree under `/output`, then wiring `test16.rs` to print the same `0`/`1` lines and path segments as the C++ program.
The module tree is in place. I’m compiling both the standalone `test16.rs` path and the Cargo project, then I’ll diff their outputs against the original executable on a broad sample set.

Implemented the Rust port in [test16.rs](/output/test16.rs:1) with the supporting module tree in [Cargo.toml](/output/Cargo.toml:1), [src/lib.rs](/output/src/lib.rs:1), [src/parser.rs](/output/src/parser.rs:1), [src/validation.rs](/output/src/validation.rs:1), and [src/path_utils.rs](/output/src/path_utils.rs:1). The parser/validators were inferred from the compiled C++ binary rather than the C++ library source, including its permissive URL validity rules, `scheme://` parsing, `stoi`-style port handling, and empty-segment-skipping path splitting.

The project builds successfully both as `/output/test16` with `rustc test16.rs -o test16` and as `/output/target/release/test16` with `cargo build --release`. I also compared the Rust binary against `/workspace/dataset/test16_executable` on a representative set of normal and edge-case URLs, and the outputs matched.
